title: The two implemented risk models use different capital ratios — 8.75% for lending markets and 8% for Real World Assets
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.5.1 sets the Capital Ratio for the lending-market model at `8.75%`, described as "the capital ratio without additional buffers." A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.2.6 completes the Real World Asset calculation by multiplying leverage-adjusted Aggregate RWA "by an 8% capital ratio."

8% is the Basel minimum total capital ratio, so the RWA path uses the unmodified regulatory number and the lending-market path uses a figure 75 basis points higher. The Atlas states no reason for the difference, and both models trace to the same source framework.

Whether it matters in practice depends on where the ratio sits in each formula, and the two placements are not equivalent. In the RWA pipeline the 8% is a genuine multiplier: RRC = adjusted RWA × 8%. In the lending-market formula the ratio appears twice, as `K × (1/CR) × EAD × ECR`, and because A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.5.3 states ECR currently equals CR, the two occurrences cancel and the 8.75% has no effect at all.

So today the discrepancy is latent rather than active — but it is a trap. The moment Sky Governance sets an ECR above CR to add a buffer, the lending-market path starts scaling by ECR/8.75% while the RWA path scales by nothing, and the two asset classes drift apart by a factor no one chose. Recording the inconsistency now is cheaper than diagnosing it later.

A related presentational hazard sits alongside it: the framework uses the same symbol for different things across models, most visibly `K` for both the Basel capital requirement (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.4) and the correlation sensitivity coefficient (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.3.3).
description: Both derive from Basel's 8% minimum, but the lending-market path applies 8.75% while the RWA path applies 8%, so identical modelled loss produces different requirements by asset class.
